title: Composer dock - the status row, the chips and file attachments
brief: The maintainer asked for the other desktop app's costaldo: the thinking/working row, the context percentage, the folder name (last segment only), the git branch when there is a repo, the session mode, and a clip that inserts files by path. Built with gentle-desk's own tokens so the six themes keep working. Two things are decided by evidence, not taste: output tokens and cost are NOT drawn because pi's RPC does not send them, and the permission mode started as a read-only label (artboard 01); artboard 02 supersedes that after the maintainer asked to change it from the UI and the L7 probe showed set_permission_mode works over the desktop channel. A file attached from outside the workspace says so, because the agent may not be able to read it.

artboards.title: A - The dock: two lines while it thinks, and the composer row
artboards.tradeoff: The reasoning row and the activity row share ONE anatomy (12px, thin glyph, time chip) so the thread does not grow a third visual language; the project name appears once and never with its full path; the branch chip disappears entirely when there is no repo instead of showing a placeholder. Cost: the working state has no separate card and no per-turn token readout, because that data does not exist in the channel - the honest alternative would be a fake number.

artboards.title: B - The session mode as a changeable control in the status row
artboards.tradeoff: A quiet text button with a caret at the right of the status row opens the four modes (Normal, Auto, YOLO, Super YOLO); YOLO and Super YOLO need an in-menu confirmation, so a risky mode costs one deliberate click and no new modal. The shown mode changes only when the channel confirms, never optimistically. Cost: it exists only while the agent works (as asked), and a sibling path refuses permission escalation while busy (escalation_while_busy) - not yet probed on this RPC method, so the failure line is a first-class state.

artboards.title: B - The session mode as a changeable control (superseded placement: the context rail's corner, sheet D)
artboards.tradeoff: A quiet text button with a caret opens the four modes (Normal, Auto, YOLO, Super YOLO); YOLO and Super YOLO need an in-menu confirmation, so a risky mode costs one deliberate click and no new modal. The shown mode changes only when the channel confirms, never optimistically. Cost per sheet D (the maintainer's pick, 2026-11-19): the control is now PERMANENT in the context rail's corner - the state exists while idle too - and menu descriptions are only the ones the channel reports (yolo, super-yolo); normal and auto carry none.

artboards.title: C - File attachments: picker, drag, chips, the outside-workspace warning
artboards.tradeoff: Attached files are chips on their own row above the text (content, not chrome); the outside-workspace case warns in amber but never blocks, because what travels is the path. On send each file is appended as its absolute path, one per line, and images keep travelling as images. Cost: the message the agent receives carries raw paths, so the thread shows them verbatim; there is no file preview.
